quest.title: Triumphant Warrior
quest.description: Through everyone's united efforts, the Abyssal calamity in the north seems to have been quelled...\nThe day of triumph draws near.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.title: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll deliver these letters to the Adventurers' Guild and The Cat's Tail! You can just handle the ones for the Angel's Share.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Phew... The expedition is finally wrapping up. I hope the maps I made on our way there are good enough to get them safely home.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, welcome back, old friend. And how should I be addressing you these days? The Honorary Knight of Mondstadt? The "Tumaini" of Natlan? Or the great hero of Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just call me by my name...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you sure have your finger on the pulse... We've barely caught our breath since Nod-Krai, but it sounds like you've already heard about what went down.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Heh, news travels fast on the wind. But before I can turn your tales into tunes, I need to hear them from the horse's mouth.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #My wine and my lyre are at the ready. So please, {NICKNAME}, take a seat and tell me your tale.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Venti everything that happened in Nod-Krai...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...Amazing, incredible! The Rächer of Solnari and The Doctor... Truly a tale for the ages!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So I'm guessing the Wild Hunt is a thing of the past now that you've defeated the Rächer of Solnari?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems that way... We were kinda focused on dealing with The Doctor, though.

choices.text: There are still some vestiges of the Wild Hunt around...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, that's good to hear. Hey, now that the Northern Abyss Calamity is finally resolved, Varka must be getting ready for the triumphant return of his expedition, right?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I haven't seen him in the longest time... He must have so many stories to share.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I was gonna ask... You two have really met before?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, Paimon was wondering about that too! He did call you Barbatos... But weren't you still fast asleep back when he was in Mondstadt?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Umm... Let's call it half-asleep. I was resting my eyes in the Thousand Winds Temple one day when I heard a commotion outside...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: It was a young knight, who had journeyed there in search of trials and oracles after hearing some tall tales at the local tavern...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: In fact, all that awaited him were moss-covered walls and an angry Ruin Guard. But he seemed completely unfazed, laughing heartily as he sent the Ruin Guard's missiles flying off into the horizons...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They must have been making quite a racket if it was enough to wake up the Tone-Deaf Bard...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Yeah... It sounded kinda like...

response.speaker: Ruin Guard
response.text: BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Hey! Is that all you've got?
Bring it on! Hahaha!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...Like that...
Giving up already? Hey, you're not half as tough as Varka said.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: A young Knight of Favonius, trekking out to the Thousand Winds Temple in search of adventure... Now there's a sight I haven't seen in a while.
Hmm? A bard in green clothes... Does this mean... you're Venti?
Hah! I was just wondering how I was gonna track you down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... So you were looking for the Tone-Deaf Bard? Strange place to start your search...

choices.text: I would have tried the Angel's Share...

response.text: Hold on — blond hair, white hair... You must be the Honorary Knight and Paimon? The Grand Master talks about you all the time.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Allow me to introduce myself. I'm Lohen, Vice Captain of the 5th Company of the Knights of Favonius and a member of the expeditionary force. Pleased to make your acquaintance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, so you're part of the expedition, huh? Right, so that's why Paimon's never seen you around in Mondstadt... Hey, wait a second! We never saw you in Nod-Krai, either!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That's probably because when the Wild Hunt was still running rampant, I spent most of my time out on my own, making mincemeat out of monsters. I barely went back to base at all.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Then, once the Wild Hunt calmed down, I got sent back to Mondstadt... Mixed blessing, if you ask me. Sounds like I missed out on some serious action.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder we never saw you while we were dealing with The Doctor... So, why did Varka send you back?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't tell me he sent you to—

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Deliver some letters.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I was gonna say deliver a letter...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: There's one for the Knights of Favonius, one for the church, another for the Dawn Winery... At least ten of them in total.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Geez... How many people has he sent to deliver his mail now? Mika, Ineffa, Lohen... He should just hire a full-time mailman already!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In fact, he's earned himself a new nickname. Let's go with... Sir Writes-A-Lot!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Another day, another nickname, huh, Tone-Deaf Bard?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehe, I'll have you know that poetry and letters were humanity's earliest means of expressing their thoughts.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: So, tone-deaf or not, I wear the title of bard with pride — and I consider "Sir Writes-A-Lot" to be quite a compliment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, really? Darn it... Maybe Paimon should come up with some harder-hitting nicknames for these two...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Anyway... Since this young man has come all the way to the Thousand Winds Temple looking for me, I assume he must have a letter for me, too. Am I right?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: You sure are. To use the Grand Master's own words:

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: "This one is for the bard in green clothes. These days, I think he goes by... Venti?"

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: "Doesn't really have an address, as such... You could start by asking around in Mondstadt. Or maybe try your luck at the Thousand Winds Temple."

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I figured that since there was this punching bag here— oh sorry, "Ruin Guard," I could get some practice in while I was at it. So, I came right here the second I got back to Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That Varka is so slapdash sometimes... It's a good thing we happened to be nearby.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So? What does the letter say?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Oh — he also said to remind you to write back.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...Nothing in particular — just some idle chatter between two drinking buddies. But if I'm supposed to write back this time... Hmm, I'll need some time to mull over my response.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Varka gave you a whole bunch of letters to deliver, right? Maybe you can head into Mondstadt and deliver the rest of them first?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: My thoughts exactly. Assuming I can find the way... Hopefully the roads haven't changed too much since the pre-expedition days?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, why don't we have Mondstadt's Honorary Knight escort this homeward-bound wanderer to the city? I'm sure some of the recipients of Varka's letters will turn out to be old friends of yours too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have no objections...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go! It's been a while since Paimon's done any guide work!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Thank you so much, Honorary Knight — and you, Miss Guide!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Abyss... The Wild Hunt... Andrius...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...Get home safe, Varka.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm... Why do my ears feel so hot all of a sudden? Is someone talking about me...

choices.text: I would have gone to The Cat's Tail...
But not enough to pose a major threat.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Surely, there's no way anyone found the secret stash of cash in my office? That would be terrible...

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Grand Master! Bad time to get distracted!

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Watch out! Enemies approaching!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, it's just a few stragglers. They're no real threat to us.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: This expedition is almost over. We just need to deal with these final few targets... and then...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We will make our triumphant return!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: He wants to test me to see if my skills have regressed? Hmph, I still haven't forgotten how he went easy on me last time!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I'm assuming you must have seen him going all out before? When the time comes, you'd better keep an eye on him for me!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Without the Rächer of Solnari to direct them, it seems like all that's left is their primal urge to destroy.

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: If this is all that the Wild Hunt can muster now, surely the Lightkeepers of Nod-Krai will be able to deal with what's left?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (Just like I thought... What we should be wary of now, is—)

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Grand Master, based on Lightkeeper intel and our own reconnaissance, one of the suspected targets should be just up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Good. You know the drill — Stay here and stand guard. Leave the rest to me.

dialogues.speaker: Knights
dialogues.text: Yes, Grand Master!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...We meet again, Andrius.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (Everything seems normal so far... Here's hoping I'm just overthinking things. There are two other places to check... Maybe this'll all go smoothly after all?)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...It's your turn, my friend.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Come, Andrius.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: ...Although if we're returning to your old home, perhaps "Andrius" is a little too ostentatious...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: Hmm, might be better to go by...
..."Boreas"?
...Boreas.
...Injustice, corruption, iniquity...
Is the surface world still as wretched and foul as ever?
Answer me, heir to the knighthood of Boreas.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh... Looks like I'm not getting out of this without a fight!

talks.objective: Read the Grand Master's letter together

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "...That's where things stand with the expedition. The victors will be returning home soon — so make sure to stock up on wine for the celebrations!"

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "P.S.: I hope everyone's keeping up with their daily training! I'll be testing you all when I get back to make sure no one's regressed."

dialogues.speaker: Varka & Lohen
dialogues.text: "P.P.S.: I wrote individual letters for each and every one of you. Don't forget to write back!" — That's all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone gets one? Wow, Sir Writes-A-Lot is really living up to his name!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: I guess the Grand Master must have something specific to say to each of us.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Even I got a letter — and I'm not a real Knight yet...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: ...Jean?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Oh... Yes, that's our Grand Master for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: By the way, anyone know where I can find the Cavalry Captain? I have a letter for him as well.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: You mean, Kaeya? He said he was meeting a friend from the church at the Angel's Share.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Allegedly for work — said he was "exchanging intel." But I'd say there's a fifty-fifty chance he's just there for a drink.

choices.text: The Angel's Share...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon bets there'll be lots of familiar faces there... How about we deliver Kaeya's letter? ...And these other two as well!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Really? That would be a great help, thank you.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Our thanks to you too, Lohen. The other knights will help distribute the remaining letters. You've had a long journey — please, go get some rest.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Great! But I won't be resting just yet. I have one last letter to deliver to Wolvendom. This one, I was planning on delivering personally.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I heard that another challenger recently passed Boreas's trial? Well, with any luck, that wolf might be willing to reveal himself to me, too...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: *sigh* ...Very well. But please remember to show respect to the local wolves.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I will. Goodbye!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Clearly, something is bothering Jean. I should talk to her before going to the Angel's Share.)

choices.text: Intelligence from the Church of Favonius?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight? You're still here?

choices.text: I'll be setting off shortly, but...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: ...Is it that obvious?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But... Varka's coming back, the situation in Nod-Krai is stable... Surely things are looking up?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: True. From what you and Lohen have told me, the expedition has indeed accomplished its strategic objectives.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: It seems that Mondstadt no longer faces any threat from the perils of the North, be they the Wild Hunt or The Doctor.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: And yet... For some reason, I can't help but recall something the Grand Master said to me before he left...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...If I don't make it back from this expedition, you'll have to assume the mantle of Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: If it comes to that, remember to train the next Knight of Boreas in my stead.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I've planted some promising seeds in Mondstadt, but they still need time to grow.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Some have yet to master the art of social interaction, some don't yet understand that they, too, need protecting, and some... Well, some might not even want to be a knight yet.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...What's wrong? Ah, there's no need to frown — I'm going on an expedition, not marching to my death! This is all just a contingency plan in the event that I'm unable to return.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Until I return, I leave them in your care.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: ...The lineage of the Knights of Boreas has nearly been extinguished twice in Mondstadt's history.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: The first wandering knight to claim the title arrived in Mondstadt a thousand years ago, along with his wolf companion.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: He was as free as the wind. He left no succession plan behind — even his name was lost to history. The title of "Boreas" could have disappeared from Mondstadt just as he did...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: But he had an informal disciple — a knight named Ravenwood, who admired the Knight of Boreas greatly. Ravenwood's valor and swordsmanship earned him the Wolf Spirit's recognition...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: ...When the old aristocracy tried to regain power, Ravenwood came once more to Mondstadt's defense. From then on, the title of Knight of Boreas was passed down from generation to generation within the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Wolf Spirit"... You mean that big blue wolf in Wolvendom?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Correct. As you may already know, the Wo{RUBY#[D]Boreas}lf of the North is the surviving spirit of an ancie{RUBY#[D]Andrius}nt god.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: And the Knight of Boreas serves as an intermediary between him and humanity.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: "Lupus Boreas, who had never known what it meant to love, came to understand it through the journey with his human companion. In the end, he chose to allow his power to become one with the land..."

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: This was once a well-known tale in Mondstadt. But these days, few people are aware that the starting point of the Wolf King's journey was not Mondstadt, but Nod-Krai.

choices.text: (Could it be...)

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: The Great Wolf King of the North came here from Nod-Krai... Although, he doesn't like to speak of his past. In fact, he rarely shows himself to people at all nowadays.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: As such, this tale can only be found deep within the Knights of Favonius Library. Even among the Knights of Favonius, few are aware of it.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: The Grand Master didn't disclose any concrete objectives before departing on his expedition. I couldn't help but wonder whether it might somehow be related to Nod-Krai's Wolf of the North...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I kept my speculations to myself, however. Sharing them would only spread unwarranted suspicion toward The Four Winds among the people of Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: You experienced the turmoil caused by Dvalin, the East Wind's actions for yourself. Surely you can understand my concern?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder Varka wasn't clear about his motives... Is that what he was worried about?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Very possibly. He was probably also reserving judgment. Having heard about your experiences in Nod-Krai, I now suspect that the Grand Master hadn't yet ascertained the true identity of our enemy at that time.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: And as it turns out, the Calamity Born in the North wasn't an ancient god, but rather the Wild Hunt and The Doctor... I guess we were both jumping to conclusions.

choices.text: Well, always better to be overprepared than caught off guard.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Yes, I completely agree. The tide can turn rapidly in times of battle. It's a leader's responsibility to prepare for every possible contingency.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Even if his contingency plan never needs to be put into action, I'm sure the Grand Master is relieved to know that it's in place.

choices.text: Facing the worst-case scenario with no backup plan would have been far worse.
(He set off from the royal court of the Seelie...)

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: You don't seem surprised... Did you sense something in Nod-Krai? Once again, you do us proud, Honorary Knight.

choices.text: It seems like there's something on your mind?

talks.objective: Leave the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: "When you're mixing drinks in hot weather, start by pouring in cold water, and add ice cubes, then drain out the water before adding the other ingredients." How's that for a secret recipe? Maybe it's worth a little intel in return?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: *scoff* Please, I've known that little trick for a good ten years at least. You'll have to offer something a little more substantial if you're serious about trading.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I know there's no one else in the tavern right now, but do you two really need to talk so loudly? Especially if you're supposed to be exchanging confidential information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaeya! Rosaria! Diluc! Paimon knew we'd find you here!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...Looks like it's about to get even noisier.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: #Haha, a little liveliness never killed anyone. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, what brings you our way?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have a letter for each of you...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You deliver Varka's letters to their recipients...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "...Please allow me to once again express my sincere condolences regarding your late father and the incident with Eroch. We make absolutely no excuse for his crimes."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "...I hope you will give some serious consideration to the question I asked you before I left — though I'm sure you're tired of hearing me ask by now. The Knights of Favonius will always welcome you."

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Hmph…

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: From the look on your face, I'm guessing the Grand Master is still refusing to drop it?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: He nags like an old man. It's hardly surprising.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Drop what? What's this about?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Nothing, really. Before leaving on the expedition, Varka came here to chat with me over a drink. I failed to avoid him.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: He asked me if I'd consider rejoining the Knights of Favonius, and I declined. He expressed his regret about everything that happened and asked me to reconsider. That's all there is to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, right... Sounds like you skipped a lot of details. There's clearly more to it!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Whatever details I chose to omit are in the past. Dragging them back up now serves no purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: You say that now, but back then, you couldn't let it go. You and the Knights of Favonius were constantly at odds.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...I wasn't seeing the full picture. I've had a lot of time to reflect since then.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: But my answer remains unchanged — I'm not rejoining the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Both the Grand Master and the Acting Grand Master are too upright and honorable.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: They can't see the shadows that lurk beneath them due to the size of the organization they lead... They need someone on the outside to keep watch vigilantly.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: If I had a Mora for every time I've heard you repeat that argument... I actually don't disagree with the first part of what you said. But don't you think someone can keep tabs on things from the inside?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: When you join an organization, you're bound by its rules, no matter how free it may seem on the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: You think so? Never mind the Knights... Have you honestly ever been bound by the rules of the Church?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Good question. Have you considered that maybe, that's why I chose to join the church and not the Knights to begin with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Um... {NICKNAME}, are they arguing or not? It's kinda hard to tell...

choices.text: They're not arguing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ohh... Kinda like the "contingencies" Jean was talking about? The more ways they have to protect their home, the better! ...Huh? {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I wonder if... this is exactly what Varka was hoping for?)

choices.text: They just have different ways of protecting those around them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: What should I report back to the Grand Master on? Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Public order inside the city, monster activity in the wild... oh, and a review of the latest vintages. Haha, I think I'll leave it at that.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: My reply won't be a long one — as usual. I'm sure Varka won't be surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: If you hadn't had to deliver that guy's mail, you wouldn't have been subjected to all this tedious arguing. When I write back, I'll tell him to quit making trouble for other people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's no trouble! Lohen did most of the work. We just volunteered to do the last leg of the journey — mostly so we could come say hello!

choices.text: Besides, I wouldn't really call that an argument.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Heh... So you see what's really going on here. All three of us fell for that old rascal's scheme far too readily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Scheme? What do you mean? Was Varka lying in his letters, then?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: No. While I'm sure Varka knows full well that Diluc would never agree to rejoin the knights, I believe the sentiments he expressed were genuine, as was his offer to welcome Diluc back.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: There are people like Kaeya and I... and then there are those who are true champions of justice to the core. Those people are the most susceptible to being driven to extremes by great upheaval... It's happened in Mondstadt before.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Not only that... But it happened to a Knight of Boreas. That'll really hit home for Varka — and that's why his nagging is even more persistent than usual.

choices.text: A champion of justice driven to extremes?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Yeah... So no one's told you this before? The lineage of the Knights of Boreas has nearly been extinguished twice in history.... The first was at its inception. The second was the case I was alluding to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Wasn't Jean telling us about this? Wait, and then we got caught up talking about the expedition, and we never got around to the second time...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I happened to hear about it from Varka once when he was drinking and started yammering on. The second crisis in the Knights of Boreas lineage... It was five hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Although the Knights of Boreas are meant to be intermediaries between humans and wolves, in practice, very few of them have been truly recognized by Lupus Boreas over the past millennium.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Of those who have, the best known are the first Knight of Boreas, Ravenwood, the "Wolf Pup" Rostam, and... hmph... Varka himself.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: But five hundred years ago, there was one who earned the respect of Boreas even before gaining the title.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: He was a disciple of Rostam. They thought he would become the mightiest Knight of Boreas who ever lived...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: He was the perfect knight. Righteous, principled... His name was Roland, the "Bloodstained Knight."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yikes... "Bloodstained Knight"? That sounds a little ominous...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Well, apparently his original title was the "White Knight."

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: But he lost countless comrades during the Abyssal calamity five hundred years ago... including his tutor and mentor, Rostam.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: The endless bloodshed stained his sword and armor a crimson as deep as black, transforming the White Knight into the Bloodstained Knight.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: After that, he threw himself completely into battling monsters, leaving Mondstadt and the Knights of Favonius behind. To this day... no one knows his final whereabouts.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: It's hard to say whether the loss of an important figure in his life is what drove him to the point of obsession, or whether he was already too far gone to save.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: But had he known that the Knights of Favonius would always welcome him back... perhaps things would have turned out differently.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: So if you want my opinion... The reason why Varka keeps asking Diluc to rejoin, despite knowing that he'll never say yes, is to let him know: You are not alone.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: ...Hmph. After all these years, he's still as persistent as ever. Just like how he used to be with me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Turns out Varka's a lot more thoughtful than he lets on... Paimon had the wrong idea about him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, there's still something about this whole Boreas business that Paimon isn't really getting. Wasn't Andrius a god in Mondstadt thousands of years in the past?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If so, why did Jean say that Boreas and the Wandering Knight only arrived here just one thousand years ago? Plus, Paimon's super curious about what happened to Roland...

choices.text: Shall we go get answers straight from the horse's — or wolf's — mouth?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a great idea! Jean said he hasn't been showing himself much lately, but he always seems happy to oblige whenever you show up! Let's go!

choices.text: We can meet up with Lohen in Wolvendom while we're at it.
You're saying, that happened to a Knight of Boreas?
You just have different ideas on how to protect Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: The Grand Master offered lots of advice in his letter regarding my recent assessments... I didn't think he'd spare a thought for that kind of thing in the middle of an expedition.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: So, um... Honorary Knight, if you have the time... do you think you could help me out with my special training?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on here? Was Wolvendom always like this? Paimon has a baaad feeling about this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt!? What are they doing here!? ...Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thank you for being such a patient listener. I feel much more settled after talking with you.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: If you have any spare time, would you mind stopping off to say hello to the other knights? I'm sure they have all missed our Honorary Knight just as much as I have.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Are you alright?

choices.text: Stay alert!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, what now? It better not be more Wild Hunt monsters...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Lohen?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew... You scared Paimon stiff! She thought you were—

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Stop right there. Answer me this — the two letters I gave you, who were they for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Two letters? Wasn't it three...?

choices.text: ...There were three.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Okay... Well, Paimon's clueless, naive expression doesn't appear to be an act...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! What are you trying to say... Wait, what are you trying to say, huh? Huh!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He's saying, you passed the test.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon passed a test? Really!? She didn't even realize she was taking one...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: You may dispense with your suspicions. The wolf pack has borne witness — they fought against the aberrations that encroached upon this land, and our attackers showed no ability to disguise themselves this time.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Ah, a familiar scent... Come, I will await you at the usual grounds.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Well, if the boss of Wolvendom has vouched for you... I guess I should apologize for doubting you just now.

choices.text: It always pays to remain vigilant.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Sure was. Fortunately, my experience in Nod-Krai didn't go to waste — turns out the Wild Hunt all feel the same when you stab them... They didn't stand a chance.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Something seems wrong with that old wolf, though... Go on, you should check on him.

choices.text: Were you attacked by the Wild Hunt, too?
Kaeya, Diluc, and Rosaria.
There's still something nearby!

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: *pant*... *pant*...

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Lupus Boreas not injured... why so weak? Am I... not strong enough?

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: You are not to blame... With your Iron{RUBY#[D]blade}claw, you successfully blocked their attacks. However... their assault went beyond the mere physical world.

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: They followed my trail from the distant north across the Ley Lines... They sought to corrupt the territory I protect. But I shall not let them succeed without a fight.

choices.text: A trail starting in the north...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...We meet again, Human Lupical.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Are you saying that the Wild Hunt we just got attacked by came all the way from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt? How is that even possible...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...As you know, I stand before you as an incomplete being. I am but one remnant of the god, Andrius's soul.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: The source of this turmoil... I can sense it. It lies in the north — It is the part of me that remains in Nod-Krai, from whence I came.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Now Paimon's even more confused! How can you be in two places at once?

choices.text: Are all gods like this?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: For many gods, housing a part of their soul within an object is no difficult feat... but those who can perform such delicate partitions as this are rare, even among the gods.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Wolf King, Andrius, was particularly adept in this art — otherwise, no remnants of his soul would have survived till the present day.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Huh? The bard's back?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tone-Deaf Bard! What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehe, maybe the God of Anemo guided me here... For it appears that someone is in need of a tale from the distant past — and our wolf friend doesn't seem too keen on recounting it himself.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Who better than a bard to do the honors? Lord Boreas, do I have your blessing to share this story?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Hmph... As you wish.

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "Lupus Boreas wandered the frozen tundra, and stumbled into the Seelie Hall. Enchanted by their song, tender as the dawn starlight, and curious about the ways of humankind, the wolf bade farewell to his home, and set off for the city to the South."

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "...As the high tower crumbled and the fierce winds fell silent, Lupus Boreas, who once had hunted with the storm winds himself, looked within and inquired: Was the shelter he provided for humanity really any different from that given by the reclusive king in his tower?"

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "The wolf entrusted those under his protection to a new god, and quietly returned to the frozen North. There, in a palace long since abandoned by its former master, the great wolf closed his eyes and slept."

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "Five hundred bitter winters passed, then five hundred equally frigid springs. He slumbered undisturbed until a knight stumbled in from the cold — just as Lupus Boreas had once done at the Seelie Hall — and woke him at long last."

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "The knight asked the wolf to join him on a journey south, to see once more the land that had all but faded from his memory. The gentle wolf, unwilling to refuse the human's earnest plea, split his soul into two halves and left his home once more."

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "Seeing how the ice and snow had given way to verdant plains, hearing the laughter and song that now filled the once-somber city, the aging Lupus Boreas turned to his friend, the God of Anemo, and remarked:"

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "'So, this is the world the humans dreamed of.'"

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "...Though the knight's journey was not yet over, the wolf chose to bid farewell to his companion here."

response.speaker: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
response.text: "He had written the end to his story. What knowledge he had been gifted flowed into the land. Everything he was, he gave unto the world."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, that's how a bard would tell the tale. Lord Boreas, is there anything you'd like to add?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...There is no need for you to ask that question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what happened... You returned to Mondstadt with that knight a thousand years ago... and then, for the sake of the new Mondstadt... you...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: You need not feel remorse on my account. That was my answer, my decision.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: If anyone should feel regret, it is the part of me who remained in Nod-Krai... I fear Andrius has not found peace in his heart even to this day.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...That is surely why those vile aberrations were able to exploit his weakness, sowing the seeds of all the turbulence that has ensued.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: But we followed Boreas's trail in Nod-Krai. We investigated and discovered no signs of instability...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Andrius should still be slumbering by the lakeside... Perhaps all the recent turmoil in Nod-Krai has had unforeseen consequences.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: And there's more — I detect another familiar scent from across the Ley Lines... a scent that reeks of blood.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could it be Roland, the "Bloodstained Knight"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, the White Knight who became the Bloodstained Knight? The mightiest Knight of Boreas? But wasn't he from 500 years ago? You think he's immortal or something?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: I remember him as just a man. His lifespan should be no longer than any other of his kind. But before he severed his connection to "Boreas," his final destination...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: It was the ancient kingdom of "Khaenri'ah," as you call it. Beyond that, I know not if he lived or died.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Khaenri'ah, five hundred years ago...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...If you want to get to the bottom of this, I'm afraid you'll have to make another trip to Nod-Krai yourselves.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: As luck would have it, another old friend of ours just so happens to be free right now... If you ask him nicely, he might give you a lift. That could save you a lot of time on the road.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Hmph... No wonder I can suddenly sense the East {RUBY#[D]Dvalin}Wind's presence.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: If even Mondstadt has been affected by the fallout, Nod-Krai must be in real trouble by now. I hope Varka can handle it.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Varka? Is he... in danger? I...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, I believe too many passengers would slow our dear friend down... I fear he only has room to carry one person... along with, perhaps, a diminutive companion.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I understand. I'll go.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Alright. Wish it could be me, but I accept that we should send our strongest warrior to fight Nod-Krai's battles.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I'll stay here and deal with any Wild Hunt that try harassing Mondstadt — it'll be a good chance to try out some new moves.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: #...I... stay in Mondstadt, too... With {NICKNAME}'s help, Varka will be safe...

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...Razor, give me your Iron{RUBY#[D]blade}claw.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Golden-haired Traveler, give this token to the current Knight of Boreas.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's this?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: It is a Wolf Spirit. It contains my power and thoughts. Though I have given him a piece before... this should bring him new strength.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Dominator of Wolves once bestowed the power of his soul upon his pack, strengthening their hearts and sharpening their claws and fangs.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...But human hearts and flesh cannot bear the soul of a wolf directly. It would be akin to forcefully merging a human and a wolf into one being... they would descend into chaos.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: To prevent the entanglement of souls, the most I can do is temporarily house my power and thoughts within cla{RUBY#[S]blade}ws and fangs wrought of steel.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Although, truth be told, that knight does not lack for power. What he needs more is the thoughts within... Hmph, but I shall leave this for him to explain.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is it safe to separate a piece of the Wolf Spirit at a time like this?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: The Great Wolf King of the North remains strong for now. Besides... Do I not have the protection of my lupical?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I... will protect lupical! The north, and Varka... I leave to you.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Just give me the word whenever you're ready, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Do you all like to split yourselves into multiple parts?
So they came from Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Any questions before you set off? Better ask now — you'll probably have to hit the ground running when you get to Nod-Krai.

choices.text: About the Wolf of the North...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The root of this turmoil lies with the remnant soul that Andrius, Dominator of Wolves and God of the North Wind, left in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: He once left Nod-Krai and braved the blizzards to confront the God of {RUBY#[S]Decarabian}Storms and claim the right to rule. Yet even as the tower fell, he chose to abandon his claim.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Instead, he returned to the North and slumbered for a thousand years, before finally journeying back — under the name of Boreas — with the first Knight of Boreas to witness the new face of Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: When the wolf's spirit could no longer maintain his physical form, Boreas chose to pour his power into the Ley Lines... with that, he became the North Wind of Mondstadt, as he is still known to this day.

choices.text: About Roland...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Five hundred years ago, Roland seemed destined to become the mightiest Knight of Boreas ever to have lived... But he was too pure of heart.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: He believed firmly in his own ideals of chivalry, vowing to eliminate all injustice from the world. But the world had never been perfect and pure, nor would it ever be.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Neither his mentor, the "Wolf Pup" Rostam, nor the Grand Master — known as the Lion of Light — could persuade him to temper his obsession.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But what was the "scent that reeks of blood" that Lupus Boreas sensed? And what is its connection to Khaenri'ah and the Abyss? Perhaps you will uncover the truth in Nod-Krai.

choices.text: About the "token" and the Wolf Spirit...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The soul of a wolf is as unyielding as ice, and Andrius is a master of molding and shaping it. His people once drew great strength and wisdom from the Wolf Spirit.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But human hearts and flesh cannot contain the soul of a god... Attempting to place the Wolf Spirit in a human vessel would slowly devour their sense of self, even if Lupus Boreas did not intend for that to happen.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's why Lupus Boreas developed the technique of imbuing weapons with his soul. It is his way of blessing his human lupical with the Wolf Spirit's protection.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: In fact, there is an ancient song that tells this tale: "A weapon once of common iron, now through friendship turned divine, twixt man and wolf a bond was made, a power born within the blade..."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehe, as much as he might claim not to accept humans, his actions sing a different tune... Oh, but keep that little observation between us, will you?

choices.text: I'm good. Let's go.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Alright. Over to you, Dvalin!

dialogues.speaker: Dvalin
dialogues.text: The Knight of Boreas awaits below. We must part ways here. Barbatos and I have other plans — we will meet you again later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... Hey, wait! How are we getting down!? Aaaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hold the line! The enemy's on the brink of collapse!

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Grand Master, it's... it's...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, reinforcements... It's about time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight reporting for duty, Grand Master!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And Paimon too!

choices.text: Let's cut to the chase.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: We're just about hanging in there. Most of their grunts are taken care of now. Their leader's gonna have to make a decision soon.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Fight or flight... What will it be, "Mightiest Knight of Boreas"?
As expected, this hastily summoned Wild Hunt horde is nothing but a disorganized rabble, a mere shadow of the forces gathered by the Rächer of Solnari.
But they have served their purpose. I now understand your tactics, and you, in turn, understand mine. This is fair... this is the way of chivalry.

response.speaker: "Roland"
response.text: Farewell, heir to the knighthood of Boreas. Whether you choose to resist me or not, I shall set right the injustices of this world... in the name of the Bloodstained Knight.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Guess they're retreating for now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that Wolf of the North lookalike... that was Andrius? But why would he be leading the Wild Hunt? And why was he talking about the Bloodstained Knight?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Forget that, we can save the details for later! He was the enemy boss, right? Are we just gonna let him get away!?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Aah, there's no point chasing after him. We've crossed blades already, and it ended in a stalemate. Right now, there's nothing we could do about him.

choices.text: Why? As strong as he might look...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: True... We're still not certain of his true identity, but whether he's a god corrupted by the Abyss, or a legendary knight...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: "Killing" him might be just about possible — especially now that you're here.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The difficult part is, we can't kill him right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you mean, is he immortal or something?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: No. Judging from our skirmishes so far, I don't think he's got any special abilities of that caliber. Nor does he have the ridiculous level of power wielded by the Five Sinners.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But compared to Rerir, our current foe clearly has a better understanding of how to exploit Nod-Krai to his advantage... particularly when it comes to Andrius's remnant soul.

choices.text: So what you're really worried about...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...But the god remains?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Exactly. Sounds like you realize what the crux of the issue is.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I managed to cut off a sample from our foe, which Albedo and Durin are analyzing as we speak. Meanwhile, our other allies should be making their way home from their own battles by now. Let's discuss this further when they're back.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...We still have some big challenges ahead before this expedition can finally be declared a victory.

choices.text: Isn't so much the enemy himself...
Surely he can't be any stronger than the foes we've fought before?
What's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I can read Varka's letter. I will try my best to write a reply.

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: A wolf's claws make poor instruments for writing human words. But that token will suffice to convey my thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I sure didn't expect my experience fighting the Wild Hunt in Nod-Krai to come in handy back here in Mondstadt. Almost makes me wonder if this was the reason I was sent back...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Also, how come that bard knows so much? And what was he doing at the Thousand Winds Temple...? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Well, whatever — I don't really care, as long as I get to do some fighting. I'm looking forward to trading blows with Lupus Boreas when he's fully recovered... I bet he'll wipe the floor with me!

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Ah, the Grand Master... The archives are filled with documents awaiting his review. I'm not letting him run off again until he's finished dealing with every last one.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: On another note... have you spoken to Jean? I hope she'll finally be able to relax a little once Varka returns.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: The Grand Master wrote in his letter that the Boom Blossom Bombs we sent worked really well — he wants to know if we've made any more...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Uncle Varka's coming home? Yay! I can't wait to go outside and play with him!

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Let me guess... you're heading to Wolvendom next? Say hi to Razor for me.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Oh — but I'm not helping him write his response to Varka. He needs to learn to be independent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Where'd this letter in our bag come from? Did it just blow in on the breeze?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's from the Tone-Deaf Bard. Apparently, he wants to hear all about our adventures in Nod-Krai... Heh, maybe we can get some tasty treats out of him in return! Come on, let's go to Starsnatch Cliff!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: ...So, you've returned from Mondstadt? Don't you want to see what it looks like now?

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: ...I was planning to take a look around there myself. Perhaps you could be my guide?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (What's this? ...An echo from a thousand years ago?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That turned into a pretty long conversation, huh? We should probably go deliver those letters to the Angel's Share now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like they're finally done "not-arguing"... Let's go ask them how they plan to respond!
